shiloh-baptist-new-site.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (New Site) and Shiloh Baptist (Old Site) are sister congregations sharing common roots stretching back to the pre-Civil War African Baptist Church of Fredericksburg. Where Old Site (801 Sophia St) has drifted toward social-gospel framing, New Site presents a cleaner mission statement: 'Glorifying God, making disciples, and serving humanity' — with 'making disciples' as the explicit Great Commission anchor. Rev. Keenan Thomas arrived in October 2022 with a Howard University / Drew Seminary education and a practical ministry background at Alfred Street Baptist (one of the largest and most Word-focused Black Baptist churches in the country). His foundational scripture — 1 Peter 4:11, speaking 'the very words of God' — reflects a high view of Scripture in praxis. The honest concern is Drew Theological Seminary, which is a theologically progressive Methodist institution — not the formation environment that produces expository complementarians. However, a man's seminary doesn't always define his ministry convictions. The 15+ ministries and Wednesday Bible study suggest an active, Word-engaged congregation. Worth visiting and hearing Rev. Keenan preach before drawing conclusions.

shiloh-baptist-old-site.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

shrine-of-the-most-blessed-sacrament-dc.assessment: The Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament is the Chevy Chase Roman Catholic parish where Justice Brett Kavanaugh is a member — he attends the 5:30 PM Sunday Mass with his family and has coached girls' basketball at the parish school. Founded 1911, the church is a large, active suburban parish of the Archdiocese of Washington under Pastor Rev. Gary R. Studniewski, with a parochial K-8 school. Theologically, the parish holds the historic Catholic positions: Nicene-Chalcedonian Christology, male-only priesthood, traditional sexual ethics, opposition to abortion. MOOP's rubric is built around Protestant confessional categories — sola Scriptura, justification by faith alone — so Catholic parishes register as yellow with a denominational note, neither green nor red. Within the Roman Catholic tradition, Blessed Sacrament is unremarkable in its orthodoxy and is a serious, traditional Catholic parish.
